chapter: Gulf Coast bands and early jobs
title: Johnny Wiggs's funeral and Raymond Burke
summary: Wiggs's private funeral, Raymond Burke, the Midway Inn and gazebo gigs, and playing with foreign musicians.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Jazz funerals: dirges, hot return, second line

blocks.x: There was no, there was a private service, you know. Yeah. His family was strange about that. They didn't want anybody to know.
They let Raymond know. They called Raymond. They called Raymond. Well, you know Raymond. Raymond will sit on his fat end, never tell anybody anything at no time. That's Raymond.
Who was Raymond?
Raymond Burke.

He's too shy to make a phone call. He played with his brother. I was talking about when I was so nervous before getting married, I didn't know what to do. I couldn't find anybody to talk to, so I called up his brother, and we talked about Raymond. Raymond played over there, I guess in Faro with him.

Oh, yes. Raymond and I first met at the Edgewater Gulf, and Raymond was playing at the Midway Inn, and I was playing with Johnny Batusi, Toots Batusi, the old man, at the Midway at another time, and Raymond came over and played some spot jobs at the Edgewater Gulf with some fiddle player. I don't quite remember his name.
I'll have to ask Raymond about that.
Raymond will tell you.
Yeah.
Raymond's older than I am. Raymond would remember better than I.
Well, he's...
Raymond's almost 80 years old. Yeah. Saw him the other day. Oh, yeah.
I run into him and his buddy Gaston Olivier. They were all...
Yeah, yeah, they were together. Yeah.
Hunting for junk.
Oh, yeah, and I was playing at the gazebo at the time.
Oh, yeah.
That was the eight hours that I played at the gazebo, and Raymond came by and said hello.
That's right. All the foreign musicians are using you now. You're playing with all the foreigners now. Sure. You told me it was...
And they're more fun.
Really?
Yes. They're more white than most of the other musicians that you play with in New Orleans.
